lines.en: I tap on Yuki’s name in my phone and wait for her to answer.
I figure that there’s a decently high chance she’s working tonight given that Sara’s bar is somehow [[probably] no longer the least successful business in all of Kumon-mi-
But I try my luck regardless as I tend to get lucky when I start monologuing. Plus, I’m curious about where things stand in the relationship between her and Yumi.
Just before I coerced her daughter into sleeping at my house, albeit for good reason, Yumi made it apparent that the two of them were talking again.
And while I highly doubt that means they’ll be going on mother-daughter spa trips anytime soon, it does mean that Yuki may have noticed something.
If I’m remembering correctly, Maki caught onto Makoto’s changes in demeanor around the time she first started acting all miserable. Before the dad thing.
It seems like aeons ago at this point, and Yuki is nowhere near as effective a mother as Maki (Which is saying a lot), but it’s still possible she’s noticed something.
: Yo. What up?
Though, I guess it’s entirely plausible that she didn’t and that we’re just going to eat ramen or something.
: I’m bored.
: Cool. The fuck you want me to do about it?
: Invite me over to hang out and make me feel young again.
: Ain’t you got like fifty girls who make you feel young every day? How the hell can I help with that?
: By not reminding me of the age disparity between us every five seconds. And by also being allowed to drink with me. And by looking old.
: Well, you don’t have to be a prick about it. But yeah, you can come chill. Sara gave me off tonight anyway.
: Was it really Sara who gave you off? Or was it me thanks to my internal narration about how convenient it would be for you to not have work right when I call you?
: Unless your weird ass brain is the one writin’ my paychecks, I’m gonna say it was Sara.
: Fair enough. Are you at Tojo Ramen?
: Nah, actually ain’t been there much lately. I’m at my apartment right now, but it’s cool if I bring people over.
: Just don’t go braggin’ about havin’ a house or some shit while you’re here or I’ll kick you in the nuts.
: I will definitely remember that. I need those and would like to keep them safe. But yeah, send me your address and I’ll head over now.
I hang up the phone and wait for Yuki to-
Nevermind. It’s here.
I let myself in after knocking on the door and hearing Yuki shout something about how her lock is broken.
It’s probably not a thing someone should be screaming about in a low-income housing complex like this, but I assume anyone who were to waltz in uninvited would be promptly beaten to death.
Also, I’m pretty sure Imani lives next door, but I’m not going to text or call her about it because I want her to hear my voice through the walls and feel confused.
: Yo. Find the place okay?
: Yeah. I’ve actually been here before.
: You stalkin’ me or some shit?
: What is it with your family and always interpreting my extreme fortune as predatory behavior?
: Idunno. Doesn’t help that you always look like you’ve been hiding behind a tree and waiting for a pretty girl to walk by or some shit.
: I’m not at that level yet, but thank you for the backhanded insult regardless. Where should I sit?
: Ain’t like you have many options. The floor or the couch. Take your pick.
: You won’t hit me if I join you on the couch, will you?
: You think I would have invited you into my apartment if I planned on beating the shit out of you?
: No. Which is precisely why I should be on guard as it would make this the perfect moment for you to strike.
: Man, can you stop treating me like I’m some kind of violent criminal? I’m an ex-junkie who just happened to have beaten the shit out of a lot of people back during my heyday.
: Ain't like I went out lookin' for that kinda shit.
: 'Sides, my lungs ain’t built for that anymore. But if you keep fuckin’ poking me about the person I used to be, I might just have to give ‘em a workout again.
: So...if I don’t stop assuming you’re a violent person, you’re going to get violent with me?
: That-
: Well...
: Of course it’s gonna sound bad if you put it that way. But really, I ain’t gonna do shit. And if you’re gonna hang out in my place, you’re gonna respect me. Got it?
: Sure. I wasn’t being serious anyway. I know that you’ll protect me if anything goes down while I’m here.
: You always been a beta or is this a new development for you?
: I’m going to ignore that and join you on the couch now.
: Need me to hold your hand and guide you over here? Or are you old enough to do it on your own, big boy?
: Please never call me “big boy” again.
I successfully and flawlessly manage to make it across Yuki’s living room without hurting myself.
However, just as I’m about to sit down, she points toward a small mini fridge underneath a desk and asks that I grab her another can of beer.
I oblige, grabbing one for myself as well. But, when I go to close the door, I accidentally shut my finger inside of it.
Thankfully, she doesn’t notice and I am able to maintain the illusion of being a strong alpha-male who will, in no way, ever submit to this woman.
: Damn. Can’t remember the last time I was alone in my own place with a guy.
Actually, on second thought, I’d probably submit to her if that’s what she wanted.
She’s surprisingly attractive when her eyes are mostly open and she’s not taking a drag of a cigarette.
The apartment does reek of smoke, of course...but I kind of expected it to given that she’s the  closest thing to a chimney I’ve ever encountered that isn’t, you know, an actual chimney.
: Feels a little different than hangin’ out at the ramen shop or the bar, huh?
: Is this the part where we make out?
: Maybe. Feel like I might need to get a permission slip from your parents first, though.
: Well, there goes the thing I said earlier about you not bringing up the age disparity thing.
: That was bullshit from the get-go. I bring that up all the time. Feels weird as fuck to be hangin’ out with a dude so much younger than me. Ain’t you young enough to be my kid?
: I feel like you’re grossly misrepresenting the gap in our ages. We’re both in our thirties, aren’t we?
: You’re in your thirties? You act like so much of a bitch all the time that I must have forgotten.
: Sometimes, I have a hard time remembering why we’re friends.
: Same here. If anything, you’re the one who should be off doin’ other shit. I ain’t gonna complain about havin’ somebody around here to help connect my oxygen tank and...
: I don’t know. Fix electronics and shit. Other stuff old people can’t do.
: Again, you are in your thirties.
: Yeah, but it ain’t like I’m gonna be there much longer. I’ll be 40 before either one of us knows it. Might as well start plannin’ my funeral now.
: If you die, it’ll be from all of the smoking and drinking, not your age.
: Amen to that, brother.
: That was me gently nudging you toward quitting.
: Gonna have to nudge a little harder than that. I ain’t givin’ up the shit that makes me happy for a few extra years of a life I’ve already made it further into than I ever should have.
: I just don’t get why you’d bother getting sober at all if you’re just going to start abusing other-
: Blah, blah, blah. Can we talk about something other than my shitty ass backstory for once? It ain’t like I’m wanderin’ around town drunk as shit. I’m in my own apartment. I ain’t hurtin’ anybody.
: Other than myself, I mean. But fuck if I don’t deserve it at this point.
: Yuki-
: Ah- nope. Don’t “Yuki” me. Didn’t I just tell you it’s about time we got together without wadin’ through all my bullshit? Hit me with somethin’ that ain’t depressing as fuck.
: But all I know is sadness.
: Well, know somethin’ else for a few minutes you fuckin’ buzzkill. Tell me your story, cause I’m tired as fuck of tellin’ you mine.
: I can assure you mine is not nearly as exciting.
: Yeah? And why’s that?
: Because I can’t remember it.
: You get smacked in the head a few too many times or some shit? Wait, do you actually have a dark past I don’t know about since I’m always the one runnin’ my mouth?
: Drugs can make your whole ass life a blur man. I’d tell you more but I’d be takin’ over the conversation again.

: It’s nothing like that. But, seeing as I am both horrible at telling stories and wouldn’t know how to tell the story in the first place, let’s just move on to something everyone can understand and appreciate-
: You ain’t gonna ask me to make out again, are-
: The two of us making out.
: You really just want me to beat the shit out of you, huh?
: Probably not in the way you’re thinking.
: Why? You like, can’t actually be into me like that, right? We’ve got nothing in common save the whole beer and ramen bullshit. Ain’t no way I’m your type.
: Well, what’s your type?
: My type?...Huh. That’s a good question.
: I don’t know if I have a type. I ain’t sure I’ve ever even thought of it before.
: I get that you’re not the romantic type, but there has to be some sort of guy you’d be into, right?
: Hmm...
: Someone who wouldn’t fuck me while I’m unconscious would be nice.
: That is...probably the lowest bar that has ever been set.
: Someone with money so I wouldn’t have to do shit and could just hang around all day. Maybe a dude with a cool bike. Tattoos.
: Maybe just me with a dick. That sounds like it would be the easiest kind of relationship.
: So basically, the exact opposite of me.
: Guess so. Surprised?
: Surprised? No. Hurt? Maybe.
: Hey, you ain’t so bad. A little soft, sure. But you’re kinda cute in like, an innocent sorta way.
: Innocent is not a word that is typically associated with me.
: Just the vibe I get. And hey, who knows? Maybe if we met like, twenty years ago or some shit, we could’ve hooked up?
: Not like I ever had much time for that kinda shit since I was always movin’ around, but I at least would’ve thought about it if you hit on me back then.
: Now, though? That’d just be weird. Like pickin’ up a kid from the candy store.
: I feel like this would have been significantly weirder if it was twenty years-
: It ain’t just about age, man. You’ve got a, like...mental age too. I’ve seen shit. Experienced shit.
: And until I learn more about whatever the fuck your deal is, it’s gonna seem to me like you’re just a kid. Or...maybe not a full on kid. But at least nowhere near as old as me.
: Plus, I ain’t gonna make you tell me your “type” or whatever, but we both know it ain’t me.
: Sure, but that doesn’t stop me from thinking you’re cute.
: Uh-huh. Sure. You think I’m cute.
: What’s really going on here? Yumi tell you I’d blow you in exchange for better grades or some shit? Spill it.
: What’s going on is I think you’re cute.
: Me.
: I’m cute.
: I look like I haven’t slept since I was twenty. At my peak, I was like, half a step above being a zombie.
: You think I’m cute. Bullshit. Not when you’re around girls like Yumi and that gyaru friend of hers all the time. They’re cute. I’m washed up. You don’t want me.
: Would it be so bad if I did, though?
: Bad? No. Just...fuckin’ weird. Only dudes who have ever tried gettin’ with me were just fuckin’ scared out of their minds I was gonna kill ‘em.
: Has that happened with other people apart from Yumi’s dad?
: Nope.
: You’ve only been with one guy?
: Can’t say that definitively as I was unconscious a fucking lot back in the day. But he’s the only one I ever, like, had a thing with.
: Dudes just didn’t see me that way. And there ain’t no way in hell you do when basically everyone you know is prettier or cuter or hotter or...you know. Other shit.
: So, funny joke, but nah. You don’t think I’m cute. And if Yumi wants good grades, she’ll suck your dick herself. I ain’t doing it for her.
: So can we make out now?
: Sure. Go ahead. Try.
: I can’t tell if that translates to “Try and I will hurt you” or “You don’t actually want to do that and I am calling your bluff.”
: Just try. All I’m sayin’.
: The closer you come, the more you’ll realize I ain’t cute at all.
: That’s not true. We’ve never really been this close before and I haven’t changed my opinion at all.
: You will. You’re fuckin’ with me.
: I’m not fucking with you.
: Yo, that’s my leg.
: Yuki, look at me.
: I am attracted to you.
: Maybe “cute” isn’t the right word for it, but it’s not like I’m just lying to get a rise out of you. And I already give Yumi good grades.
: This is such a weird way to admit to me that my daughter is sucking your dick.
: She’s- no. What? I give her good grades without making her work like that for them.
: She’d probably work “like that” for them if you asked. But good on you, I guess. Also, get your hand off of my leg. I’m starting to think you’re serious.
: I am.
: Wha...why the fuck are you trying to act all cool all of a sudden?! The hell’s gotten into you, man?
: I can be cool when I want to be.
: There also wasn’t a wall for me to slam my hand against, so this will have to do.
: That one sentence just took away like 50%% of the coolness on display here.
: Yeah, well no one’s perfect- and that includes you.
: You do look like you haven’t slept since you were twenty.
: You’re pale, your breath smells like smoke, and your hair is a weird shade of blonde that probably needs to be bleached again.
: Well, fuck you too dude.
: I am also very intimidated by your presence and am fully aware you could kick my ass whenever you want.
: But, should you ever decide to stop thinking I’m just fucking around with you-
: I’d be honored to be the first person you ever decide to have recreational sex with.
: I think this is the part where we make out.
: I...kinda do as well, but...
: I’ve got some bad news for you.
: What kind of-
: Yo! I’m here. Your lock still busted?
: Oh, shit. I forgot she was a part of the opening monologue.
: Uhh...yup! Come on in!
Yuki’s affection has increased to [yuki_love]!
